c8_gallery_pt_error.split_sum_diagnostic: the split sum against shadeIblReference without occlusion (every 32nd sample, 1,024 samples a strategy; the reference's own noise not measured): gold 0.656, red plastic 0.326, car paint 0.489, velvet 0.153, brushed steel 0.174, thin film 0.514. Rows where the frame's error is far above the split sum's (brushed steel, velvet) point to missing transport, mostly the sky occluded by neighbouring spheres; rows where both are high (thin film, car paint, gold) carry image-lighting model error too.
c8_gallery_pt_error.prediction_check: I predicted 0.2 to 0.5 with low confidence and the glass row carrying most of the error. Both were wrong: 0.68, and the thin-film and car-paint rows carry more than glass.

development_runs: Before addendum A: pixel-area tracer 1.81 at 64 and 1,024 samples, unchanged by tessellation 64 x 32 to 512 x 256; coverage 0.976 by the any-against-centre count. A NaN in the sheen evaluation (a local direction a hair longer than 1, from a frame built on a float normal) was found at 1,024 samples and fixed by normalising local directions before the evaluation.
does_not_prove: That the tracer is right where these checks do not reach (caustics through near-specular glass); anything on a GPU; that the raster's model is wrong in a way the split sum alone explains.
